answer: Each agent registers an opal‑signed credential bound to a quartz‑anchored vault that records the hash of its payment source and timestamped heartbeat. The gale protocol continuously cross‑references these vaults, merging any credentials that share a vault, source hash or identical heartbeat pattern into a single kin‑linked identity, and rejecting new nodes that duplicate any link. An attacker must purchase a distinct payment source, generate a unique vault key and maintain a separate timing stream for every fake node, inflating cost linearly with the number of Sybil identities.
